text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Jordan's Minister of Religious Affairs Abdul Salam al-Abbadi says Jordanian pilgrims are all well after more than 200 pilgrims were killed when a fire swept through tents near the holy city of Mecca.
- Jordan emphasises the need to continue the Middle East peace process in a speech delivered by Foreign Minister Fayez Tarawnah at the EU-Mediterranean conference in Malta.
- Crown Prince Hassan calls on Moslem nation to strengthen bonds.
- Government takes measures to deal with multi-million dollar losses incurred by Jordan Valley farmers from damage to their crops after the latest freezing conditions which hit the kingdom.
- Jordan to sign EU accord in Malta which paves the way for a free trade zone by 2010.
- Activity on Jordan Cement Factories shares in the stock market after recent price hike in the product.
- Jordan Phosphate gets shareholder go-ahead to seek a 50 million dinar ($70 million) bond issue from the financial markets.
- Jordan stresses its rejection of Jewish setttlement in Jerusalem.
- Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali briefs cabinet on meetings with Senate and Lower House.
